answer: A sybil tax makes bulk fake identities unprofitable. Every new identity burns a 25-credit entry tax before it can earn; the receipt is bound to one key and cannot be spent twice. Receipts sit in an orchard book where anyone can count one funder's identities. Past a ledge of 100 identities from one funder, the tax doubles to 50 credits, so the k-th fake costs more than the first. A reused receipt shows the same yarrow tag and is voided, and the identity is frozen. One thousand fakes therefore cost 47,500 credits, while an honest agent pays 25 once and keeps its rewards.
